about: Ready posts to swap into calendar.json (same format). Swap: copy a post over an existing one and keep that one's n, day, date and weekday. Then run check-calendar.mjs.

posts.caption:
Dish drop is a weekly thing now on this page. Weekly-drop energy, minus the countdown panic: one real scan, out in the open, every week.

This week: the steak board. No diagonal camera angle, no zoom quietly lying to you about size.

Share karoge ya akele rakhoge?
posts.alt: Dish drop week 1: a real steak board scanned in 3D.

slides.h: One plate. Whole spotlight. *This week only.*
The steak board. *No angles. No lies.*
slides.b: Real scan. True size. Zero filter.

slides.h: Share it, or *keep it to yourself?*
slides.b: Comment A or B. No judgment. (Some judgment.)

posts.caption:
Week 2 on the pass: the steak sandwich, stacked exactly the way it lands on your table.

One question before you order: whole lunch, or shared starter? Fight about it in the comments.
posts.alt: Dish drop week 2: a real steak sandwich scanned in 3D.

slides.h: One person's lunch, or *two people's starter?*
slides.b: Real scan. True size. You decide.

posts.caption:
Dish drop, week 3: the green plate. Look at that colour before you say anything.

Rate it out of 10. Decimals allowed if you're that person.
posts.alt: Dish drop week 3: the green plate, a real dish scanned in 3D.

slides.h: Out of 10. *No half marks.*
slides.b: Real scan, every angle, zero mercy.

posts.caption:
Dish drop, week 4: the trio, lined up, real size, no crop trick making it look bigger than it is.

Tag the two people this is going straight to. Only two, choose wisely.
posts.alt: Dish drop week 4: the trio, three real dishes scanned in 3D.

slides.h: Three of them. *Tag exactly two people.*

posts.trend: "Is it worth the hype" review culture (§2, §3)
posts.caption:
Food vloggers taste-test after they've already paid. We do the sight test before you order anything.

Read the menu line, picture the size in your head, then swipe and see how wrong you were.

Pehle andaza lagao, phir dekho, bas honest rehna.

Comment "close" or "way off". No in-between.
posts.alt: The sight test: guess the size from the menu line, then see the real steak sandwich.

slides.h: Everyone taste-tests after. *We sight-test first.*
Guess the size. *No peeking.*
Real size. *How far off were you?*

posts.trend: "Is it worth the hype" review culture
posts.caption:
Sight test, round two. The menu says "steak board, served with sides", five words doing a lot of heavy lifting.

Picture it, then swipe for the actual board. Be honest about how off you were.
posts.alt: Sight test round two: guessing the steak board size from the menu.

slides.h: Round two. *Guess the board.*
The whole board. *Called it, or nah?*

posts.trend: Worth-the-hype reviews + launch queues (§1 points 2 and 7)
posts.caption:
Lahore's national pastime: standing in a queue for two hours, then telling everyone whether it was worth it.

We'd rather you knew before the bill shows up, not after. See the actual plate, then decide: worth it or not?

Hype pe nahi, plate pe faisla karo.
posts.alt: Text post: is it worth the hype? Decide before you order.

slides.h:
"Is it actually worth the hype?"
*We'd rather you knew first.*
slides.ru: Hype pe nahi, plate pe faisla karo.

posts.when: evergreen · good after any big Lahore opening
posts.caption:
New place, queue around the block, 45 minutes of waiting, and then everyone decides in 30 seconds because the waiter is standing right there.

The wait was never the problem. The panic order at the table is.

Table milte hi QR scan karo, plate dekho, phir order. Line ka badla aise lo.
posts.alt: A group chat about waiting in a restaurant queue and then panic-ordering at the table.

slides.h: Long queue. *Panic order.*
slides.title: Dinner plan

msgs.t: queue is literally around the corner
waiter aa gaya. kya order karein??
ruko QR scan kar raha hoon, size dekh lo pehle
ok THAT'S how we do it

posts.trend: The "is this even real?" doubt, AI imagery everywhere (§1 summary)
posts.caption:
"Is this even real?" is a fair question when half your feed was never actually cooked.

Every dish here is a scan of a real plate, from a real kitchen, on a day someone actually plated it.

Asli plate, asli size, koi AI nahi, kasam se.
posts.alt: A real steak sandwich, scanned in 3D, not AI generated.

slides.h: "Wait, is this even real?" *Yes. Every pixel.*
slides.b: A scan of an actual plate. No AI touched this.

posts.trend: "Expectation vs reality" meme format, done honestly (§2)
posts.caption:
Expectation vs reality, MENVA edition. Twist: it's the same photo.

That's the whole point of a real scan before you order, no gap between the ad and the plate.

Umeed aur haqeeqat, dono aik hi plate.
posts.alt: Expectation vs reality: the trio, shown twice, exactly the same both times.

slides.h: *Expectation.*
Reality. *Plot twist: also this.*
slides.b: Umeed aur haqeeqat, is baar dono aik hi plate hain.

posts.caption:
Every dessert counter in Lahore is suddenly an expert in kunafa chocolate. Some bars are properly thick. Some are... optimistic.

You only find out which one you got after you've already paid and cut into it.

Dessert menus deserve a sight test too. Restaurants: think about letting guests see the actual bar at true size before they order. DM "PILOT".

Pehle dekho, phir cut karo.
posts.alt: Text post about the Dubai chocolate trend and sight-testing dessert menus.

slides.h: Suddenly, everyone sells *Dubai chocolate.*
slides.ru: Pehle dekho, phir cut karo, warna regret guaranteed.

posts.caption:
Every bakery in Lahore insists theirs is the original three milk cake. Soaked right, glossy, perfect slice, and on the menu they all sound identical.

Next time, see the actual slice on your table before you order it. Let the cake defend itself.

Teen doodh, ek sawal: kitna bara slice milega?
posts.alt: Text post about the three milk cake trend and bakery claims.

slides.h: The *"original"* three milk cake, again?
slides.ru: Teen doodh, ek hi sawal, slice kitna bara milega?

posts.caption:
Single, double, triple smash. The menu gives you three words and lets your imagination do the rest.

The size jump between "double" and "triple" is the one thing you actually want to know before you commit, not after the food coma.

Send this to the friend who always orders triple and never learns.

Double lein ya triple? Dekh ke faisla karo.
posts.alt: A joke receipt comparing single, double and triple smash burger regret levels.

slides.h: Single, double, triple. *Pick your regret level.*
slides.title: Smash burger receipt
slides.footer: MENVA, see it before the damage is done.

posts.when: Pakistan match nights (post manually on the day)
posts.caption:
Match night at a restaurant: every eye is on the screen and the menu is basically decoration.

Order the platter before the toss so nobody's flagging down the waiter during the powerplay. Priorities.

Toss se pehle order, baqi sab match ke baad.
posts.alt: Text post for Pakistan cricket match nights.

slides.h: Order before the toss. *Argue after.*
slides.ru: Toss se pehle order kar lo, baqi drama match ke baad.

posts.caption:
Ammi at home: "ghar pe khana hai, bahar kyun jana hai."
Ammi at the table: "yeh 'aioli' kya hota hai, beta?"

Stop translating the menu word by word. Tap the dish, put it on the table, let her see it herself.

Tag the friend who's the designated menu-translator at every family dinner.
posts.alt: A phone notes screenshot about explaining a menu to parents at dinner.

slides.h: Things I explained to my parents tonight
slides.title: Friday, 8:47 pm
items: just showed him the AR instead

posts.caption:
Family dinner out: twelve people, three generations, and one person who's been silently elected to order for the whole table.

Show Nani the plate before it lands and you skip the entire "yeh kya mangwa liya" routine.

Tag the one who always orders for the whole table.

Nani ko pehle dikha do. Phir koi shikayat nahi.
posts.alt: Text post about ordering for a big family dinner with multiple generations.

slides.h: Twelve people, three generations, *one designated orderer.*
slides.ru: Nani ko pehle dikha do. Phir koi shikayat nahi.

posts.trend: "Tell me you're from Lahore without telling me" format (genz-culture.md)
posts.caption:
Tell me you're from Lahore without telling me.

We'll go first: you judge a restaurant by the portion before you've even tasted anything.

Your turn, drop yours in the comments.
posts.alt: Text post: tell me you are from Lahore without telling me.

slides.h: Tell me you're from Lahore *without telling me.*
slides.b: We'll start: portion size gets judged before taste does.

posts.caption:
Student budget rule one: you do not gamble the week's food money on a dish you've never seen.

If one dinner is eating half your allowance, at least see exactly what's coming before you commit.

Budget tight hai? Pehle dekh lo, phir kharcha karo.
posts.alt: Text post: student budget rule one, see the dish before you spend on it.

slides.h: Never pay full price for *a surprise.*
slides.ru: Budget tight hai? Pehle dekh lo, phir paisa kharcha karo.

posts.caption:
Lahore's got rooftops, neon signs, flower walls, a whole industry built around the photo-worthy spot.

We think the best photo right now is your own table, dish already floating on it before the food's even out of the kitchen.

Place it, screenshot it, post it. Camera pehle khata hai, this time literally.
posts.alt: A phone showing the green plate placed on a table in AR, before the real dish arrives.

slides.over: New photo spot, zero rooftop required
slides.h: Forget the rooftop. *Table's the spot now.*
slides.b: Place it, screenshot it, post it before the food even arrives.

posts.trend: Launch queues fade; proof lasts (§1, §5 risks)
posts.caption:
Opening week hype fades fast: the queue photos stop, the reels slow down, and by week six your menu is doing the selling on a normal Tuesday night.

Give it the real plate to work with: true-size 3D scans, on every table, every night, not just launch week.

DM "PILOT". Lahore pilot: PKR 25,000.
posts.alt: Text post for restaurant owners: opening-week hype fades, but the menu keeps selling.

slides.h: Opening week ends. *Your menu is what's left.*
slides.by: Give it something real to sell with.

posts.trend: Food vloggers as the trust layer (§1 point 7)
posts.caption:
A food vlogger's verdict travels further than anything you post yourself, fair. But they show up once, film for twenty minutes, and leave.

Your guests are there every night, deciding off a menu that's mostly adjectives. Let every one of them run their own sight test: the real dish, true size, before they say yes.

DM "PILOT" for the Lahore pilot.
posts.alt: Text post for restaurants: let every guest run their own verdict before ordering.

slides.h: A vlogger visits once. *Your regulars, every week.*
slides.b: Let every one of them see the plate before they order.
